children: Indian auto parts maker Hero Motors' (HERT.NS) $104.2 million IPO was fully subscribed on the first day of bidding on Wednesday, exchange data showed, led by demand from retail investors.

Hero Motors received bids for 95.3 million shares worth about 8 billion rupees ($83.36 million) as of 2:40 PM IST, or 1.08 times the 88.6 million shares on offer, exchange data showed
The firm is led by Pankaj Munjal, whose family also runs India's largest two-wheeler maker by volumes, Hero MotoCorp
Qualified institutional buyers bid for 0.01 times the shares reserved for them, while non-institutional and retail portions were subscribed 0.84 times and 1.79 times, respectively
Hero Motors allocated shares worth 3 billion rupees to anchor investors at 84 rupees apiece, the upper end of the IPO price band, ahead of the IPO opening
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to 6 billion rupees and an offer for sale worth up to 4 billion rupees
Proceeds will be used for debt reduction and expand a manufacturing facility
IPO activity remains strong with listings planned by top bourse National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI.NS)
